agency.name: Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry, Bureau of Workers' Compensation

ttd.basisLabel: Gross average weekly wage before taxes
ttd.rateText: Indemnity equals two-thirds of the weekly wage with statutory minimum and maximum adjustments (Workers' Compensation Act § 306(a), 77 P.S. § 511). 2026 schedule: AWW $774.43 or lower = 90% of AWW; $774.44 to $1,045.50 = $697.00; $1,045.51 to $2,091.00 = 66 2/3% of AWW; $2,091.01 or more = $1,394.00.
ttd.minText: No fixed dollar minimum: workers with an AWW of $774.43 or less receive 90% of their AWW; between $774.44 and $1,045.50 the rate is a flat $697.00 (2026 schedule).
ttd.periodLabel: injuries occurring on and after January 1, 2026 (statewide average weekly wage $1,394.00, Act § 105.1)

waiting.text: Indemnity is payable from the eighth day if disability lasts more than seven calendar days but less than 14 days; the first seven days are not payable unless disability lasts 14 days or more (Act § 306(e), 77 P.S. § 514).

ttdDuration.text: Total disability benefits may last indefinitely while the employee remains unable to work; after 104 weeks of total disability the employer may request an impairment rating evaluation, and a whole-body impairment under 50% converts benefits to partial disability, payable for a maximum of 500 weeks (Act § 306(a.3), § 306(b)).

ppd.text: Partial disability is paid at two-thirds of the wage loss, for a maximum of 500 weeks (Act § 306(b)). Specific losses (amputation or permanent loss of use of body parts, eyes, hearing, disfigurement) are paid for a set number of weeks under the schedule in Act § 306(c), 77 P.S. § 513.

facts.text: Pennsylvania uses a four-band rate schedule: low-wage workers receive 90% of their wage, a middle band receives a flat amount ($697.00 in 2026), and only the upper band receives two-thirds of wages.
Indemnity must be paid (or the claim denied) within 21 days of the employer's knowledge of the injury; late payments carry 10% interest.
Indemnity may be offset by unemployment compensation (injuries from 8/31/93), employer-funded pensions (from 6/24/96) and Social Security old-age benefits.
The 2026 statewide average weekly wage also sets the medical fee update: payments for treatment from January 1, 2026 rise by 3.5%.
